messages:
customer-jdoe: Hi team — we keep getting partial streaming responses then a reconnect loop from our frontend. Happens after ~90s of idle. No error body, just SSE stops sending final chunks and the client reconnects and replays the request. Billing spike for that user. Can share request-id: req_0a1b2c3d.

support-engineer: sorry about that, looking. Do you see 502/504 from our side or just connection drop? Any repro steps?

customer-jdoe: No 502, connection just silent. The browser console shows 'EventSource connection lost'. We tested behind Cloudflare (pro) + ALB in front of origin. Repro steps: 1) POST to /v1/chat/stream with valid token 2) stream starts streaming partial tokens 3) idle (no new tokens) for 90s 4) final chunk never arrives, client reconnects and server processes replay. I'll paste a curl repro.

customer-jdoe: ```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d '{"model":"rwd-medium","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"long-windup test"}],"stream":true}' 
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream
```

samir: thanks, can you attach a full HAR or the edge request id? req_0a1b2c3d should map to our access logs.

customer-jdoe: attached HAR (link) and we captured tcpdump between CF and ALB.

dev-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-314. Tagged support/escalation and eng-runtime.

infra_oncall: quick notes — ALB default idle timeout is 60s, many teams set to 120s. Cloudflare also has origin keepalive semantics that can cause half-close. Which LB mode are you using (proxy vs TCP)?

customer-jdoe: ALB (http/1.1) fronting an ECS service. Cloudflare in front of ALB. We suspected ALB+CF interaction.

alyssa: from our logs (linked) I see the connection from CF to ALB is staying open but ALB sends FIN after 90s of inactivity. There's evidence of ALB tearing before we flush final chunk. Also saw "upstream prematurely closed connection" in our origin nginx.

support-engineer: can you confirm you're not gzip-encoding SSE? gzipping can force proxies to buffer. Also any intermediate WAF?

customer-jdoe: we're not gzipping SSE response, content-type is text/event-stream. No custom WAF rules.

samir: two likely culprits: 1) ALB idle timeout vs Cloudflare origin timeout mismatch causing half-close, 2) Nagle/TCP PSH edge where last small chunk is coalesced and not flushed. Workarounds: increase ALB idle timeout to 180s, send periodic SSE heartbeats (\n: keepalive\n), or switch Cloudflare to "disable http2" for that route to avoid h2 windowing.

customer-jdoe: we can try heartbeat header. We already send a newline every 30s from app to keep alive but still saw drop at 90s.

alyssa: can you share exact bytes of heartbeat event? Some proxies ignore comments if not strictly newline terminated. Example heartbeat payload that worked in another case: ```
: hb

```

customer-jdoe: used `
: ping

`, same pattern. Strange.

infra_oncall: another angle — Cloudflare has a configurable 'origin keepalive timeout' of 100s; if CF closes while ALB still expects, you can see silent half-close. Also ALB's deregistration/drain can close connection mid-stream. Any ECS tasks rolling?

customer-jdoe: no rolling, single task during repro.

support-engineer: we pulled traces for req_0a1b2c3d — our runtime processed the request and wrote final bytes, but nginx reported EPIPE when flushing to ALB. Suggests ALB closed socket early.

samir: propose quick repro: - bypass Cloudflare using host header to ALB directly, run curl from external host to ALB to see if disconnect still occurs. If it disappears, CF <-> ALB interaction is likely.

customer-jdoe: ran direct-to-ALB test — same behavior but timeout moved to ~65s. So ALB is definitely closing.

alyssa: confirm ALB idle timeout: looks like a custom setting at 60s in your account. That matches 65s observed (plus RTT). So ALB kills connection before final event. That explains missing final chunk and replay.

customer-jdoe: ok, if ALB closes, why does the client replay and server recompute (billing)? Shouldn't we detect idempotency?

support-engineer: our API treats streaming chat as non-idempotent by default. Reconnects are seen as new calls unless client replay layer dedupes. Also some clients re-open with same payload which we bill. We can add guidance for clients to use dedupe keys or idempotency keys for streaming endpoints to avoid double billing on reconnects.

samir: short-term mitigation for you: set ALB idle timeout >= max expected idle (recommend 180s) and enable our streaming keepalive header: `x-rwd-stream-keepalive: 30` which tells our runtime to emit heartbeat events. Also consider switch to NLB TCP passthrough (preserves TCP semantics, less proxy buffering).

customer-jdoe: changed ALB to 180s and re-tested — streaming completes consistently now, no replay. Billing spike resolved on quick test.

support-engineer: awesome. We'll add a follow-up doc: best-practices for SSE across Cloudflare+ALB/Envoy/Nginx, include recommended keepalive interval and ALB timeout combo.

dev-bot: INC-2026-314 updated: resolved-by-customer-change-to-alb-timeout.

cloudflare-bot: Note: if you still see gaps, enable 'Origin Keep-Alive (Improved)' in Cloudflare UI or open ticket to extend origin timeout.

customer-jdoe: thanks everyone — please add note about idempotency keys for streamed requests in the docs, that'll save others.

alyssa: will draft. Key takeaways: 1) ALB default idle timeout can cut final chunks 2) Cloudflare/ALB mismatches can create half-close behavior 3) gzip/content-encoding and http2 can induce buffering 4) recommend keepalive events and idempotency keys.

support-engineer: closing thread after docs PR. If you see recurrence, reopen and we'll escalate to infra team for deeper tcp level traces. :thumbsup:
